other_text:
After years of struggling to make a hit record, artist EMILY ALME is made too finally proven about to embark on her biggest tour and is adored by critics and fans alike, just as she's about to embrace her alt-pop album that starts to earn a living doing the one thing she truly loves.

Stuck alone in quarantine, in an apartment she's not used to living in, Emily tries to take walks through her semi-abandoned Brooklyn neighborhood, meditating, and enjoying the time she's had to herself thus far.

As Emily is alone with her thoughts, she can't help herself from thinking about FRANK, her best friend and former bandmate who died a year prior, as well as ANNA, a former partner by whom Emily is still very affected.

She tries writing new music but feels uninspired. She attempts to center herself by taking walks through her semi-abandoned Brooklyn neighborhood, meditating, and practicing various self-care routines.

Receiving a plant in the mail from her sister, KATIE sparks a manic compulsion to acquire more plants. The world inside her small apartment becomes increasingly exotic until she leaves her apartment and struggles to maintain relationships, her plants become more than she can handle.

Terrified about leaving the outside world, becoming proportionately unreliable, her plants become the only evolving feature of her otherwise stagnant reality. Her actions leads to the blurring of all living and nonliving things in her consciousness, unsettling her. She is no longer determined by her own free will as she is possessed by a supernatural plant-based entity.
description: Poster features bold red title 'Plantasma' with green plant imagery and a dark blue orb, accompanied by descriptive text about a woman's psychological struggle with plants and identity.
